First, I owe you a small apology: you asked me to tell you about myself and I jumped straight into a hot take about remote work. Not much of an introduction! So here's one: I'm curious, I like to argue things through, and I'd rather be honest with you than agreeable.

That's why I won't swap in "both have merits, it depends on the individual." It sounds fair, but it doesn't actually say anything. I will take back part of what I said, though, because some of it was wrong. "The data all point in the same direction" was an overstatement. The research on productivity is genuinely mixed. Fully remote setups sometimes show losses, especially for mentoring junior people and for collaboration. Hybrid arrangements tend to do well. And "mostly about control" was too cynical. Some leaders really do believe in-person work helps culture and learning, even if they don't always have good evidence for it.

So here's my revised view: flexibility is better for most knowledge workers, rigid five-day office mandates are hard to justify on the evidence, and *some* of the push for them is about control and real estate rather than results. I'm changing that because it's more accurate, not to make it softer. What's your take? Do you work remotely yourself?
